slides.title: Charting the Growth of Social-Physical HRI (spHRI): A Systematic Review Pipeline Augmented by Small Language Models
slides.highlight: This research evaluates using small language models to accelerate the screening of social-physical human-robot interaction literature, supporting the development of embodied social robots in RwB.

card.one_liner: Small language models can augment systematic reviews by recovering relevant papers missed by human screeners.
card.key_idea: A pipeline using a unanimity ensemble of four locally deployed SLMs (≤1.5B parameters) as a second-pass filter for title and abstract screening in spHRI research.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on 32,000 records; the SLM ensemble identified 39 additional relevant papers (10.29% of final set) missed by humans, operating orders of magnitude faster.
card.limitation: SLMs cannot replace expert judgment due to a precision-recall tradeoff and binary outputs lacking confidence scores.

slides.title: When Robots Rate Their Own Interactions: Engagement Validity and the Strangeness Failure
slides.highlight: This research explores 'inverted evaluation' where LLM-powered robots rate their own interactions, providing insights into the boundary conditions of using AI to assess human-robot interaction for RwB.

card.one_liner: LLM-powered robots can accurately rate interaction engagement but systematically fail to detect human strangeness/discomfort.
card.key_idea: An 'inverted evaluation' framework where LLMs complete standardized HRI questionnaires from the robot's perspective using interaction transcripts and multimodal context.
card.evaluation: Tested via HRI-CUES dataset (5 LLMs, 1,522 evaluations) and a Nao robot pilot (N=4). Metrics included Pearson r and ICC.
card.limitation: LLMs lack access to internal affective states, conflating philosophical engagement with comfort and failing on unexpressed strangeness.

slides.title: EmotionAI: A Privacy-Preserving Computational Intelligence Pipeline for Speech-Emotion-Grounded Conversational Analysis
slides.highlight: This work presents a local pipeline integrating speaker diarization and emotion classification for grounded conversational analysis, supporting HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and diarization.

card.one_liner: A fully local, privacy-preserving pipeline integrating speech emotion recognition with LLM-based grounded conversational analysis.
card.key_idea: Combines pyannote diarization, Whisper ASR, and wav2vec2 SER with an adversarial three-model local LLM panel for timestamp-grounded, citation-constrained question answering.
card.evaluation: Zero-shot RAVDESS testing (48.8% accuracy), a 12-question human rubric study, and CPU runtime benchmarks (mean 157s). Results show significant cross-corpus fragility.
card.limitation: Poor zero-shot transfer (especially 'Sad' class), limited ecological validity using acted speech, and small-scale human evaluation.

slides.title: GROVE: Grounded Pedestrian Simulation via Natural Language for Interactive Social Robot Navigation
slides.highlight: GROVE enables the generation of realistic, socially challenging pedestrian simulations via natural language, which helps narrow the sim2real gap for social robot navigation. This is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: GROVE is a text-to-scenario framework that generates realistic, grounded pedestrian simulations for social robot navigation training.
card.key_idea: Combines LLMs with RAG-based behavior tree generation, Theta* global planning, and Social Force Models to bridge semantic intent and physical navigation.
card.evaluation: Qualitative trajectory analysis and VLM-based scoring (GPT-5) against Text-Crowd and TRACE across hospital, office, and residential environments.
card.limitation: High computational inference costs and an inability to handle dynamic environmental changes like moving furniture.

slides.title: voxmap-studio: An open-source speaker diarization annotation tool with built-in cost instrumentation
slides.highlight: This tool provides a framework for annotating speaker diarization data and measuring the cost of human correction, supporting the development of diarization models relevant to HyECHO.

card.one_liner: An open-source speaker diarization tool that quantitatively measures annotation cost via edit-operation counts and time.
card.key_idea: React-based tool featuring automatic initialization, uncertainty-based highlighting, and a confirmation-gated export process using "phantom" attention checks to ensure ground-truth verification.
card.evaluation: Preliminary study on nine AMI audio files comparing manual vs. assisted annotation; found uncertainty-highlighting most cost-effective and accurate.
card.limitation: Small sample size with a single annotator, limiting statistical conclusions and the separability of meeting difficulty from condition.

slides.title: Neural Speaker Diarization via Multilingual Training: Evaluation on Low-Resource Nepali-Hindi Speech
slides.highlight: This work evaluates EEND-EDA and DiaPer architectures for speaker diarization in low-resource Nepali-Hindi speech, contributing to HyECHO's focus on diarization and social perception.

card.one_liner: DiaPer outperforms EEND-EDA in speaker diarization for low-resource Nepali-Hindi speech, especially in multi-speaker scenarios.
card.key_idea: Comparing EEND-EDA (LSTM-based) and DiaPer (Perceiver-based) architectures trained on a multilingual corpus of English, Nepali, and Hindi speech to improve cross-lingual generalization.
card.evaluation: Evaluated using DER on LibriSpeech, VoxCeleb, and NeHi test sets. DiaPer showed superior performance in 3, 4, and mixed-speaker settings.
card.limitation: Evaluation relied on synthetically generated multi-speaker recordings rather than real conversational audio, potentially limiting real-world applicability.

slides.title: BiPACE: Bisimulation-Guided Policy Optimization with Action Counterfactual Estimation for LLM Agents
slides.tldr: IMPROVED ADVANTAGE ESTIMATION FOR LLM AGENTS
slides.highlight: BiPACE improves long-horizon LLM agent training by using behavioral clustering and action-conditioned baselines to fix credit assignment mismatches. This is relevant to MIMIC's use of LLM-based agent models for societal-scale simulation.

card.one_liner: BiPACE improves LLM agent RL by replacing observation hashing with behavioral clustering and action-conditioned baselines.
card.key_idea: BiGPO clusters actor hidden-states via cosine distance to reduce singleton groups, while PACE uses action-conditioned peer baselines to estimate a nonparametric Q(s,a) - V(s) advantage.
card.evaluation: Tested on ALFWorld, WebShop, and TextCraft using Qwen2.5 (1.5B/7B). BiPACE Q outperformed GiGPO and GRPO, reaching 97.1% success on ALFWorld/7B.
card.limitation: Currently evaluated only on text-only environments with discrete action spaces and uses a fixed cosine radius.
